title: Kernel telemetry annotation guidelines and observability cookbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary

Purpose: establish a consistent, low-overhead telemetry and annotation scheme for kernel-level events in the Redwood serving runtime so engineers can rapidly correlate performance anomalies to code, scheduling decisions, and hardware signals. This doc is a practical cookbook: schema, tagging rules, example dashboards, alert mapping, and step-by-step triage flows.

Scope
- Applies to all production and pre-production runtime kernels (attention kernels, kv-cache manager, batching scheduler, device transfers).
- Includes: span/tracing annotations, metric labels, log enrichment, histogram buckets, and example dashboard panels.
- Excludes: application-level business traces (those belong to product services).

Why this matters
- Kernels are the primary source of per-token latency variance. Without consistent annotations you cannot correlate tail latency to kernel selection, quantization path, or NUMA placement.
- Standardized telemetry reduces mean time to triage (MTTT) for SREs and runtime engineers and enables automated regression detection.

OWNER & ROUTING
- Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime (runtime-observability subteam)
- Oncall routing: runtime-sre -> page if P0, slack #runtime-observability for P1/P2 context.

Telemetry primitives (schema)
- Traces/spans: all kernel entry points must emit a trace span with the following tags (attributes):
  - span.name: kernel.<family>.<op> e.g. kernel.attention.forward, kernel.kvcache.fetch
  - kernel.version: semantic version of kernel binary (e.g. 2025.10.3)
  - model.variant: redwood/gptq-7b-q4
  - quantization.path: fp16|int8|gptq
  - device: gpu-0|gpu-1|cpu
  - shard_id: shard-<id>
  - scheduling.policy: fair|priority|batching
  - batch_size: integer
  - seq_len: integer (input sequence length for this request)
  - kernel_rows_processed: integer (work metric)
  - kvcache.hit: true|false
  - fallback.triggered: true|false (if a higher-latency fallback path was used)
  - enqueue_time_ms: numeric (time spent waiting in software queue)

- Metrics: expose the following (Prometheus naming conventions recommended):
  - kernel_duration_seconds{kernel_family, kernel_op, device, model_variant} histogram
  - kernel_enqueue_seconds{...} histogram
  - kernel_work_units_total{...} counter
  - kernel_error_count{...} counter
  - kernel_qcache_hit_ratio{model_variant, shard_id} gauge (0..1)

- Logging: structured JSON logs at INFO/ERROR with fields: ts, span_id, trace_id, span.name, kernel.version, device, shard_id, batch_size, seq_len, msg. Avoid freeform stack traces in INFO.

Annotation rules (do this for every kernel entry/exit)
1) Small, deterministic tags only: prefer short keys (<=20 chars) and low-cardinality values. High-cardinality values (request_id, user_id, prompt_hash) should be attached only to span logs, not as metric labels.
2) Device and shard must use canonical identifiers (gpu-0..gpu-N, numa-0..). Mapping table maintained in /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/team-wiki/shard-id-lookup.
3) Quantization path: annotate all internal kernel branches that change numeric width. Use the canonical set: fp32, fp16, int8, gptq.
4) Scheduler policy: annotate the policy decision that scheduled the kernel run. If multiple policies applied, include the resolved policy and a comma-separated policy_stack attribute.

Sampling & cardinality controls
- Default sampling: 1% of all traces for production traffic; 100% for traces with kernel_duration_seconds bucket > 0.99 (99th percentile) or if fallback.triggered=true.
- High-variance buckets (seq_len > 2048 or batch_size > 64) must be sampled at 10% by default.
- Retention: raw traces retained for 14 days; aggregated histograms 90 days.

Recommended histograms & buckets
- kernel_duration_seconds buckets (seconds): [0.0001, 0.0005, 0.001, 0.002, 0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.5]
- enqueue_time_ms (ms): [0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500]
- These buckets are optimized for sub-1ms kernel latencies while still capturing pathological multi-second stalls.

Example instrumentation snippets
- C++ (span creation with OpenTelemetry):

  // create span at kernel entry
  auto span = tracer->StartSpan("kernel.attention.forward");
  span->SetAttribute("kernel.version", "2025.10.3");
  span->SetAttribute("model.variant", model_variant);
  span->SetAttribute("quantization.path", "gptq");
  span->SetAttribute("device", device_id);
  span->SetAttribute("shard_id", shard_id);

- Python (metrics export example):

  from prometheus_client import Histogram, Counter
  kernel_duration = Histogram('kernel_duration_seconds', 'Kernel latency', ['kernel_family','kernel_op','device','model_variant'])
  kernel_duration.labels('attention','forward','gpu-0','redwood/7b').observe(0.00072)

Telemetry enrichment and cross-product correlation
- Correlate model-level request traces (API spans) with kernel spans via trace_id. Ensure API-side instrumentation adds trace_id and root.span_id to request metadata so downstream kernel spans inherit it.
- Add a consistent prompt_hash tag (sha1 of normalized prompt) in the API span only. Kernel spans should reference prompt_hash only in logs, not as metric labels.

Dashboards: canonical panels (Grafana recommended)
- Kernel overview panel (heatmap): kernel_duration_seconds heatmap by kernel_family vs device; group by model_variant.
- Tail-latency waterfall: stacked bars showing enqueue, kernel, kvcache_fetch, device-transfer contributions for 50/90/99/99.9 percentiles.
- Scheduler policy impact: boxplots of kernel_duration_seconds by scheduling.policy.
- KVCache hit map: time-series of kernel_qcache_hit_ratio by shard_id.
- Regression indicator: change-point detector that compares 24h median kernel_duration_seconds to 7-day baseline; raises warning at >15% and P0 at >50%.

Example alerting table
| Alert name | Signal | Threshold | Severity | Runbook link | Owner |
| Kernel-tail-latency | kernel_duration_seconds 99.9p aggregated over 5m | > 60th baseline * 2 (or > 200ms absolute) | P1 | /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/kernel-high-tail-latency | eng-sre |
| Scheduler-queue-buildup | rate(kernel_enqueue_seconds_count[5m]) increasing & queue length > 200 | sustained 5m | P2 | /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/scheduler-queue-eviction | runtime-oncall |
| Fallback-rate-spike | ratio(fallback.triggered) > 1% | 1m | P0 if > 5% | /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/fallback-investigation | runtime-sre |

Triage playbook (step-by-step)
1) Detect: alert fires and oncall is paged.
2) Initial gather (5 min): collect: relevant traces, last 30m histograms, scheduler queue lengths, device-level metrics (GPU SM utilization, PCIe transfer latency), and kernel.version across hosts. Use the Diagnostic bundle collector: /scripts/collect-kernel-diagnostics.sh --trace-id <trace> --since 30m.
3) Correlate: find top kernel_family and kernel_op contributing to 99.9p. If enqueue_time_ms dominates, jump to scheduler playbook. If kernel_duration_seconds dominates, check kernel.version and quantization.path.
4) Isolate: toggle canary routing to an alternative kernel variant (if available) or pin model to previous kernel.version. For Dedicated clusters use: rctl route update --model <id> --kernel-version <previous>.
5) Mitigate: scale up capacity on the affected shard pool or switch routing policy to lower-latency fallback.
6) Post-incident: capture a regression report with before/after histograms and root cause. Link to regression in the changelog: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/release-notes/kernel-version-changelog.

Example diagnostic CLI outputs (simulated)

  $ collect-kernel-diagnostics.sh --since 10m
  HOST      GPU  kernel.attention.forward.p50  kernel.attention.forward.p99  enqueue-ms
  g-12-01   0    0.00072                      0.0048                       0.8
  g-12-02   1    0.00068                      0.0069                       4.2

Ownership & release rules
- Any kernel change that touches scheduling or quantization must include telemetry coverage: a signed checklist in the PR template (see PR checklist section below). Telemetry must be present in unit/integration tests prior to merge.

PR checklist (required fields)
1) Telemetry emitted for kernel entry/exit with required attributes.
2) Prometheus metric names and histogram buckets documented in PR description.
3) Load test run attached (link to perf run) demonstrating no >5% regression in median or 15% in 99.9p.
4) Reviewers: runtime + observability + performance owners.

Sample PR description snippet

  Telemetry: Emit span "kernel.attention.forward" with attributes [kernel.version: 2026.01.1, quantization.path: gptq, shard_id].
  Metrics: kernel_duration_seconds histogram (buckets: [..])
  Load test: https://perf.redwood.internal/runs/98765

Common troubleshooting patterns and fixes
- Symptom: 99.9p up but median stable.
  - Likely causes: device interference (noisy neighbor), sporadic kernel fallback, or small sample of large seq_len. Check kernel.version mismatch across hosts and fallback.triggered logs.
- Symptom: uniform latency increase across all percentiles.
  - Likely causes: resource saturation (GPU SM, memory bandwidth) or a model-level regression. Check device utilization and recent model rollout.
- Symptom: enqueue_time spikes without corresponding backend kernel duration increase.
  - Likely causes: scheduler misconfiguration or queue starvation. Apply scheduler debug flags and collect queue histograms.

Appendices
A) Example trace JSON (span-level)\n{
  "trace_id": "abcd1234efgh",
  "spans": [
    {"span_id":"s1","name":"api.request","attributes":{"prompt_hash":"...","model_variant":"redwood/7b"}},
    {"span_id":"s2","name":"kernel.attention.forward","attributes":{"kernel.version":"2026.01.1","device":"gpu-0","shard_id":"shard-7","batch_size":8,"seq_len":512,"kernel_rows_processed":1024}}
  ]
}

B) Common PromQL snippets
- 99.9p kernel latency for attention forward across GPUs:
  histogram_quantile(0.999, sum(rate(kernel_duration_seconds_bucket{kernel_op="forward",kernel_family="attention"}[5m])) by (le, device))
- Percent of kernels hitting fallback:
  sum(rate(kernel_error_count{reason="fallback"}[1m])) / sum(rate(kernel_work_units_total[1m]))

C) Migration notes for legacy telemetry
- Existing legacy spans (pre-2025) used keys like "kernel_type" and "lat_ms". A migration adapter will translate legacy keys to the canonical names for 12 months; new code must use canonical names immediately.

Contacts and escalation
- Runtime observability owners: Aisha Patel (author), Diego Martinez (runtime-sre), Evelyn Zhou (profiling).
- Pager: runtime-oncall (P0/P1). Slack: #runtime-observability.
